intro:
Monitoring the gold price in Canada today gives investors, collectors, and jewelry buyers a real-time view of precious metal valuations in Canadian dollars. As one of the world's premier gold-producing nations and home to the globally respected Royal Canadian Mint, Canada boasts a deeply liquid precious metals market where bank counters, bullion dealers, and specialty jewelers track the live spot rate around the clock.

Whether you are checking the Canada gold rate today to buy 24K Canadian Gold Maple Leaf coins, comparing the 22K gold price Canada per gram and per 10 grams for bridal jewelry, or calculating the melt value of 18K and 14K rings, our live tables and interactive calculator above provide accurate CAD quotes across every standard weight and purity.

sections.h2: Gold Rate in Canada Today: How Live CAD Spot Prices Work per Ounce and Gram
paragraphs: When you check the gold price today Canada tables on this page, you are viewing the global wholesale bullion benchmark converted continuously into Canadian dollars (CAD). Because international bullion trading clears primarily in US dollars while Canadian dealers and banks settle transactions in loonies, the live canada gold rate reflects two simultaneous feeds: the global spot price of fine gold and the real-time USD/CAD currency exchange rate.

In the Canadian bullion and banking sector, the troy ounce (approximately 31.1 grams) is the primary benchmark unit used to quote coins and wholesale contracts. At the same time, retail jewelry stores, pawnbrokers, and small-bar buyers across Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Calgary, Edmonton, and Ottawa rely on the gold price in Canada per gram and per 10 grams for everyday transactions. For larger portfolio allocations, the 1 kilogram bar (1000 grams) serves as the standard institutional unit.

Keep in mind that the figures shown in the live chart represent unfabricated wholesale metal. When buying physical coins at a Canadian bank branch, ordering assay-carded bars from a bullion dealer, or shopping for finished jewelry, the final retail price includes minting costs, dealer premiums, and applicable provincial or federal taxes on non-exempt items.

sections.h2: Which Gold Purity to Buy in Canada: 24K (9999 Fine), 22K, 18K, and 14K
paragraphs: Canada has set the global benchmark for ultra-high-purity bullion through the Royal Canadian Mint, which pioneered 99.99% pure 24K gold (often called four-nines fine or 9999 fineness) for standard investment coins and bars, and has even produced special issues at higher purities. In Canada, virtually all domestic investment bars, wafers, and Gold Maple Leaf coins are struck in 24K (9999 fine) gold, making 24K the undisputed standard for Canadian bullion investors.

In the cultural and bridal jewelry market, the 22K gold price Canada today is widely tracked across the Greater Toronto Area, Metro Vancouver, Calgary, and Montreal. Stamped with a millesimal fineness of 916, 22K gold contains twenty-two parts pure gold blended with two parts strengthening alloy, delivering the deep, unmistakable yellow luster cherished for traditional South Asian, Middle Eastern, and East Asian wedding ornaments.

For mainstream Canadian retail jewelry, engagement rings, and everyday chains, 14K gold (585 fineness) and 18K gold (750 fineness) are the dominant choices. Because pure 24K metal is too soft to hold prongs securely in harsh winter climates and active daily wear, Canadian jewelers favor 14K for maximum scratch resistance and affordability, while luxury boutiques offer 18K for customers seeking richer color saturation.
bullets: 24K (9999 fine): The signature Canadian bullion standard used in Royal Canadian Mint Gold Maple Leaf coins and wafers.
22K (916 fine): High-purity traditional jewelry alloy prized across Canadian multicultural bridal and heirloom markets.
18K (750 fine): Fine designer jewelry standard offering a warm golden hue with dependable structural strength.
14K (585 fine) and 10K: Durable, weather-resilient alloys popular in mainstream Canadian mall and boutique jewelry stores.

sections.h2: The Royal Canadian Mint, Gold Maple Leaf Coins, and Buying from Canadian Banks
paragraphs: One unique advantage of the Canadian market is the accessibility of sovereign bullion through both specialized precious metal dealers and major Canadian commercial banks. The flagship product of the Royal Canadian Mint is the Canadian Gold Maple Leaf coin, struck in 99.99% pure 24K gold. Recognized worldwide for its purity and advanced security features—including precision radial lines and a micro-engraved laser maple leaf privy mark—the Maple Leaf is among the most liquid bullion coins on Earth.

While 1 oz Gold Maple Leaf coins carry a slightly higher fabrication premium over spot than cast bars, their advanced anti-counterfeiting technology and sovereign backing make them effortless to resell at any Canadian bank bullion desk or coin dealer. The Royal Canadian Mint also produces 9999 fine gold bullion bars in 1 oz and 1 kilogram sizes, alongside popular minted wafers from accredited global refiners.

When comparing bank bullion counters (such as TD Precious Metals, Scotiabank, RBC, or CIBC) with independent Canadian bullion dealers, investors should look closely at both the purchase price and the buy-back policy. Some banks offer discounted pricing to existing account holders with convenient branch pickup or insured home delivery, while specialized bullion dealers often stock a wider selection of fractional gram bars and international coins with competitive spreads.
bullets: The Royal Canadian Mint Gold Maple Leaf is struck in 99.99% pure (24K) gold with micro-engraved laser security features.
Major Canadian banks and independent bullion dealers both sell physical 1 oz coins, fractional coins, and certified bars.
Royal Canadian Mint 1 oz and 1 kg bullion bars carry high liquidity and universal recognition across North America.
Keep minted bars and wafers sealed in their original assay cards to qualify for top buy-back rates when selling.

sections.h2: GST/HST Tax Rules on Investment Gold vs. Jewelry in Canada
paragraphs: Understanding Canadian federal and provincial sales tax rules is essential before making any precious metal purchase. Under the Canadian Excise Tax Act, precious metals qualifying as financial instruments—specifically gold bars, ingots, wafers, and coins minted with a purity of at least 99.5% pure gold (which includes all 24K 999 and 9999 bullion)—are completely exempt from the federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) as well as the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) and provincial sales taxes across Canada.

However, this tax exemption strictly applies to high-purity investment bullion of 99.5% fineness or higher. Coins minted at lower purities—such as 22K foreign bullion coins that contain only 91.67% pure gold—generally do not meet the Canada Revenue Agency's 99.5% purity threshold for precious metal financial instruments, meaning they can attract GST/HST at checkout. That is why Canadian investors overwhelmingly favor 24K (9999 fine) Gold Maple Leafs, Gold Buffalos, and 9999 fine bars over 22K coins.

Finished gold jewelry of any karat—whether 14K, 18K, 22K, or even 24K wearable ornaments—is treated as a retail consumer good rather than an exempt financial instrument, and is therefore subject to standard GST, HST, or provincial sales tax depending on the province of purchase.
bullets: Gold bullion bars, wafers, and coins with a purity of at least 99.5% (24K) are exempt from GST and HST across Canada.
24K Canadian Gold Maple Leaf coins (99.99% pure) qualify for full GST/HST exemption nationwide.
22K gold coins (91.67% pure) fall below the Canadian 99.5% tax-free purity threshold and may be subject to sales tax.
All retail gold jewelry—including 22K bridal pieces and 18K/14K rings—is subject to applicable provincial GST/HST.

sections.h2: Gold Weights Used in Canada: Troy Ounces, Grams, 10 Grams, and Tolas
paragraphs: Because Canada uses the metric system for daily commerce while participating in the North American wholesale bullion market, buyers routinely navigate both troy ounces and metric grams. When checking the gold price today Canada 1 oz, the weight always refers to one troy ounce, which equals approximately 31.1 grams. Fractional Gold Maple Leaf coins are also minted in half-ounce, quarter-ounce, tenth-ounce, and twentieth-ounce denominations, as well as 1 gram Maplegram sheets.

In retail bullion bars and jewelry showrooms, metric weights are standard. Investors can purchase certified 24K wafers in 1 gram, 5 grams, 10 grams, 20 grams, 50 grams, and 100 grams, as well as 1000 gram (1 kilogram) cast bars. Using the 1 gram and 10 gram rows in our live table makes it easy to compare the per-gram cost of a 10 gram wafer against a full 1 oz coin.

Across thriving cultural shopping districts in Brampton, Mississauga, Scarborough, Surrey, Vancouver, Calgary, and Edmonton, shoppers frequently ask for the 22k gold price in Canada per 10 gram or per tola (approximately 11.66 grams). Many families also compare the gold price in Canada vs India or Dubai when planning weddings, using our live tables to evaluate raw metal rates before factoring in local making charges and taxes.
bullets: 1 Troy Ounce (31.1 grams): The standard benchmark unit for Canadian Gold Maple Leaf coins and bank bullion quotes.
1 Gram and 10 Grams: Widely used for minted gold wafers, scrap gold evaluations, and 22K jewelry pricing.
1 Tola (11.66 grams): Traditional weight unit frequently referenced in Canadian South Asian jewelry boutiques.
1 Kilogram (1000 grams): Low-premium institutional cast bar weight favored for large portfolio allocations.

sections.h2: Why Local Canadian Dealer and Jewelry Prices Differ from the Spot Rate
paragraphs: The live spot rate shown on financial screens represents the wholesale baseline for large institutional delivery bars before fabrication. When you buy a 1 oz Gold Maple Leaf coin or a 10 gram wafer in Canada, the dealer adds a premium over spot to cover refining to 9999 purity, precision minting, security packaging, insured armored shipping, and retail operating costs. Fractional items like 1 gram bars carry a noticeably higher percentage markup per gram than 1 oz coins or 100 gram bars.

When shopping for 22K, 18K, or 14K jewelry in Canadian stores, the retail price is built from several layers above the raw karat melt value. In traditional 22K jewelry stores across the Greater Toronto Area and Metro Vancouver, jewelers typically quote the daily 22K gram rate, multiply it by the net gram weight of the ornament, add a craftsmanship making charge (which varies depending on whether the piece is machine-made or intricately handcrafted), and then apply GST/HST.

Furthermore, each dealer maintains a bid-ask spread—the difference between the price at which they sell metal to you and the price at which they buy it back. Comparing both the selling premium and the buy-back rate across Canadian banks and bullion shops ensures you keep transaction friction to a minimum.
bullets: Bullion dealer premiums cover 9999 refining, minting, tamper-evident assay cards, and insured Canadian delivery.
22K cultural jewelers in Canada price ornaments by gram weight plus a separate labor making charge plus GST/HST.
Mainstream 14K and 18K retail jewelry carries flat piece pricing that reflects design, branding, and showroom overhead.

sections.h2: What Moves the Gold Price in Canada: The Loonie, Bank of Canada, and Global Markets
paragraphs: The gold rate in Canada today is shaped by the interplay between global bullion demand and the strength of the Canadian dollar. Because Canada is a major exporter of crude oil, minerals, and natural resources, the Canadian dollar often behaves as a commodity-linked currency. When global risk appetite weakens, oil prices soften, or the Bank of Canada cuts domestic interest rates relative to the US Federal Reserve, the Canadian dollar can depreciate against the US dollar—which directly boosts the CAD price of gold for Canadian holders.

As a result, physical gold held in Canadian dollars has historically demonstrated low volatility and reliable purchasing-power protection during domestic economic slowdowns. Even on days when the US dollar spot price moves sideways, a weaker loonie will push the live gold price in Canada higher on local dealer boards.

Global macroeconomic forces—including central bank reserve accumulation, persistent inflation, sovereign debt expansion, and geopolitical tensions—provide the broader trend for precious metals. Because gold is also a major component of the Canadian mining sector on the Toronto Stock Exchange, domestic investors closely watch the live CAD ounce price to gauge both physical bullion values and mining equity margins.

Bank of Canada interest rate policy and domestic inflation trends influence local demand for hard assets.

sections.h2: Practical Tips Before Buying or Selling Gold in Canada
paragraphs: Under Canada's Precious Metals Marking Act, while quality marks on jewelry are voluntary, any karat stamp applied to an article (such as 10K, 14K, 18K, 22K, or 916) must be accurate within strict legal tolerances and must be accompanied by a registered Canadian trademark or a recognized foreign hallmark. When buying jewelry in Canada, always inspect the clasp or inner band for clear purity and maker stamps, and request a written invoice detailing the karat purity, exact gram weight, and making charges.

For bullion investors in Canada, sticking to 99.99% pure (24K) products such as Royal Canadian Mint Gold Maple Leaf coins or LBMA-accredited 9999 gold bars guarantees GST/HST exemption, tight buy-back spreads, and instant dealer verification. Store bullion in protective capsules or original sealed assay cards, as surface scratches or opened packaging on 24K gold can reduce a dealer's buy-back offer.

If you are selling old 10K, 14K, 18K, or 22K jewelry in Canada, sort your pieces by karat stamp, weigh them on a digital gram scale at home, and use our live CAD calculator above to find their exact intrinsic melt value. Get quotes from reputable bullion dealers or established refiners rather than mall kiosks to maximize your payout.

Handle 24K bullion coins by their edges only and keep them in protective capsules, as pure gold scratches easily.

faq.q: Is gold bullion exempt from GST and HST in Canada?
faq.a: Yes, provided the gold meets the Canada Revenue Agency's purity requirement of at least 99.5% pure gold. All 24K (999 and 9999 fine) gold bullion bars, wafers, and Canadian Gold Maple Leaf coins are completely exempt from GST, HST, and provincial sales taxes across Canada, whereas 22K coins and all retail gold jewelry are taxable.

faq.q: Why is the Canadian Gold Maple Leaf coin minted in 9999 fine (24K) gold?
faq.a: The Royal Canadian Mint introduced the 99.99% pure (four-nines fine) standard to create one of the purest sovereign bullion coins in the world. Containing virtually zero base metal alloy, the 24K Gold Maple Leaf qualifies as a tax-exempt financial instrument in Canada and enjoys instant liquidity worldwide.

faq.q: Can I buy physical gold directly from banks in Canada?
faq.a: Yes. Several major Canadian chartered banks operate retail precious metals programs that sell 24K Gold Maple Leaf coins and certified gold bars online or through local branches, alongside specialized independent Canadian bullion dealers.

faq.q: How does the Canadian dollar exchange rate affect the gold price in Canada today?
faq.a: Global wholesale gold is priced in US dollars, so the live gold price in Canada is calculated by converting the USD spot price into Canadian dollars at the real-time exchange rate. When the Canadian dollar weakens against the US dollar, the CAD price of gold rises even if the international USD spot rate is unchanged.

faq.q: How is 22K gold jewelry priced in Canadian stores?
faq.a: In specialty 22K jewelry boutiques across Toronto, Brampton, Surrey, Vancouver, and Calgary, pieces are typically priced by multiplying the net gram weight by the store's daily 22K gold rate, adding a per-gram or flat making charge for craftsmanship, and then adding applicable provincial GST or HST.

faq.q: What is the difference between 1 troy ounce and 10 grams when buying gold in Canada?
faq.a: One troy ounce equals approximately 31.1 grams and is the standard weight for flagship Gold Maple Leaf coins and wholesale bullion quotes. Ten-gram wafers and per-gram rates are metric units widely used for smaller investment bars and retail jewelry valuation.

faq.q: How do I calculate the scrap value of 14K or 18K jewelry in Canadian dollars?
faq.a: Separate your jewelry by karat stamp, weigh the metal in grams (excluding gemstones), and multiply the weight by the live 14K or 18K per-gram CAD rate in our table above. Scrap buyers will pay a high percentage of this melt value minus a modest refining margin.
